blockers.wanted: a distant rumble with some audible body above 100 Hz so a brightness knob does something
blockers.tried: low-pass filter 80..800 Hz mapped to a brightness macro; thunder at 1.8 km is already 99% under 200 Hz, whole-sound centroid ~38 Hz
blockers.workaround: claim passes (35 -> 39 Hz) but the knob is nearly inaudible by measure; kept it

blockers.wanted: to know whether the thunder node's built-in air absorption makes a following air node double-count
blockers.tried: first used thunder -> air (2400 m), which left only a 23-70 Hz band; dropped air
blockers.workaround: thunder alone plus a low-pass and an fdn reverb

wishlist: thunder field for rumble brightness / a high-cut independent of distance
a way to trim leading silence length from distance without changing the rumble (an `at` negative or a start-offset on the thunder)
a measure that reports 'time of first sound' directly in summary (leading silence is there but only in listen)
what_worked: thunder node alone gave silence-then-clap-and-rumble at once (leading silence 5.1 s, centroid 38 Hz, -60 dB decay 7.6 s)
macro claims verified with a sweep in one call
